As a leaf develops in the spring, its green chlorophyll enables it to use the sun's energy to turn carbon dioxide and water into sugars. This process is called photosynthesis. The sun is brighter and the days longer in summer, so the leaves do their main work then. They turn more of the sun's energy into sugars. The leaves make and store more chlorophyll-sugars for use when they lose their leaves in the fall and need energy to sprout in the spring.

Human beings store energy, too. We eat vegetables with lots of chlorophyll and get their energy. We store this energy as fat. Yuck!

There is a different chemical in a leaf's cells called carotene that color the leaf yellow. The green chlorophyll doesn't show through the carotene because it's not making as many sugars. In the fall, the energy-making days are over and the chlorophyll disappears. So can the energy (fat) we stored "disappear" if we're careful in the fall?

Maybe I can work off those extra foods (alcohol, ice cream, pumpkin pie) I eat - so I have some energy to go on vacation in the spring."

Jay Ochoa is an Associate Professor of English at the City College of San Francisco where he teaches creative writing. He shot the red lighthouse light with a weak smile until the pained look in the woman's eyes on the couch grew too obvious.

The woman turned to her husband and began to speak to him. He stooped to meet her glasses and she laid her hand on his thigh. The saleswoman retrieved her microphone.

"We're fine in here!"

The woman from inside made a small sign of gratitude and then turned down the volume on the camera crew's speakers. The husband's near sobbing had become her unwelcome center of attention.

The steady sound of crashing waves from the front door gave Mira a moment of peace. She turned to the couple on the couch, and asked them if they were alright.

The young woman answered for them. "Grandpa and Grandpa are doing fine. They've been fine for a long time now."

Jonas had been here once before, in the spring, but it hadn't looked like this. Then winter was still here and the water in the river was high, washing against the top of the dam. He had watched chubby mayor Duffy marooned on his island while the town shed tears about the rising water.
Mists and the warm light of morning made Jonas feel so comforted he began to sing. He crossed his waterfall footbridge and began to walk on the suburb side of the stubble. Jonas looked at his flashlight, and his map, and considered alternate paths to more shelters. They will find their way home,

Only when the time came to write home did Mira realize that her experiences never went the way she anticipated!
